ops-broadcast: :mega: ANNOUNCE: New maintenance & SLO policy + scheduled cross-region simulated failover + loadtest. Please read and ack.

ops-broadcast: TL;DR: Starting Mon 2026-06-21 we'll activate a new "quiet-window" policy for planned maintenance and run a simulated failover + loadtest on Tue 2026-06-22 04:00-05:30 UTC across prod regions. Purpose: validate graceful-degradation, autoscaler behavior, and the new tiered SLO windows.

ops-broadcast: What changes (policy):
- Quiet-window: during planned maint windows we will relax p99 alerting to a tiered threshold rather than mute alerts. Tiers: critical services (p99 <= baseline*1.3), core infra (p99 <= baseline*1.5), best-effort (p99 <= baseline*2.0).
- Any tier breach will create a P0 if accompanied by >3% error-rate increase.
- Quiet-window is applied only to on-call paging rules; dashboards/graphs unaffected.

marta: Why this change? We've had alert fatigue during maintenance and it's masked real regressions. Tiered thresholds let us reduce noise while still surfacing true issues. Also lets product teams plan for safe maintenance.

josh: Loadtest plan outline:
- 04:00 UTC: start synthetic traffic injection (gradual ramp to 1.8x normal qps over 15m)
- 04:30 UTC: trigger regional failover simulation (shift 30% traffic away from target region)
- 04:50 UTC: scale down target pools to simulate partial capacity loss (simulate node drain)
- 05:10 UTC: recover traffic and restore normal routing
- 05:25 UTC: post-mortem probes + light regression suite

rachel: Safety gates:
- Abort & rollback if global error rate >2% for 10m OR p99 > tier*2 for 10m
- Autoscaler caps: max-burst set to 2.0x for the test to avoid runaway.
- Deploy-bot will pause between major steps and emit `test:checkpoint` events.

oncall: Oncall coverage: I'll be primary for the test. @rachel you'll be fallback. Please confirm coverage windows. Also please set Slack DO NOT DISTURB for non-oncall engineers during the test window.

marta: Noted. I'll publish the schedule to #all-hands and add a short blurb for customers (status page pre-incident style) in case SDKs see transient errors. Suggested message: "Planned resilience test: you may see short transient errors; no data loss expected."

josh: Quick ops tips: watch KV-cache miss rates and open connections per host. If connection churn > baseline * 1.2, throttle synthetics and pause failover step. Use: `make monitor test-guard` to open the guard dashboard.

oncall: Will add a temporary SLO window entry for the test in the SLO service (start/end) to avoid noisy paging; still record metrics for post-test SLA analysis.

infra-bot: Scheduled job: resil-test-20260622 queued. Canary region: eu-west-1 at 04:00 UTC. Step delays: ramp=900s, failover=1200s, drain=1200s. Notifications will be posted to #ops-log.

rachel: Post-test expectations: 1) short summary (1-3 bullets) posted here, 2) metrics snapshot attached to the incident doc, 3) follow-up action items assigned in sprint board within 3 working days.

marta: Please ack here if you'll be watching during the window or if you need coverage arranged.

ops-broadcast: Final note: this is a company-level resilience exercise; expect some noise but no risky infra changes. If you're not oncall and see alerts, please wait for oncall instructions before acting. We'll circulate the runbook and rollback playbook in #eng-sre tomorrow. :rocket:
